projects.title: Malawi Floods Emergency Recovery Project
implementors: MoFEPD — Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning and Development, Malawi
DoDMA — Department of Disaster Management Affairs, Malawi
projects.beneficiaries: community; household; low-income households; vulnerable population; producer; women; children
projects.rationale: "The project was prepared in response to the 2015 floods" ... "The MFERP constituted a set of multisectoral interventions in response to the flooding's wide-scale damage and loss. The project prioritized restocking and provision of immediate food items and restoration of livelihoods for the affected households and key strategic assets including secondary roads, education and health facilities, riverbank protection, water supply systems, and irrigation schemes."

MoFEA — Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs, The Gambia
projects.rationale: "The aim of the PPCR Project grant was to assist developing countries like The Gambia to build resilience to the impacts of climate change by preparing and implementing a robust strategic investment plan."

projects.title: Drought Resilience and Sustainable Livelihoods Programme DRLSP-IV Eritrea
projects.beneficiaries: pastoralist/herder; community; smallholder farmer; female-headed households; women; youth
projects.rationale: "The overall goal of this Programme was to build communities' resilience to drought and Climate Change, improve their livelihood and promote regional integration in the Horn of Africa." The programme built water mobilisation and livestock infrastructure and the capacity of populations and governments "to better cope with the effects of climate change, resources scarcity and conflicts related to natural resources utilization".

projects.title: Climate Resilient Agriculture in three of the Vulnerable Extreme northern crop-growing Regions of Namibia (CRAVE)
projects.lead: EIF — Environmental Investment Fund of Namibia
implementors: MAWLR — Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform, Namibia
projects.beneficiaries: smallholder farmer; community; vulnerable population; subsistence farmer; household; low-income households; women
projects.rationale: "The Project Theory of Change was that with adequate climate information and training, participating communities would become more resilient against the shocks and impacts of climate change. Traditional agricultural practices would also need to be transformed through the introduction of climate resilient agriculture, conservation agriculture practices, action oriented research and the introduction of improved seed varieties" ... "The project was therefore designed to introduce sustainable water supplies to these farming communities through solar water pumping."
